root_idea.summary: The root has two divergent semantic orientations: gathering and falling, demolition, or abasement.
root_idea.development: The gathering branch extends from gathered wool to flocks and human companies. The falling branch extends to earth removed from wells, collapse, destruction, death, and the loss of power or standing. These root-level developments do not make every branch a meaning of every derived form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under its normalized lexical form ثُلَّة.

senses.definition: A gathered company or group of people.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expressions ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ and ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ, it denotes a company or group of people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or pour earth back into a grave or well after it has been dug.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is earth used to refill the excavation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour forth money, or to remove and empty what is in a receptacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence includes pouring out pieces of money and taking out the contents of a container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a gathered portion from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a classical construction with ثُلَّة understood as a gathered portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dislodge, break, or dig into a collected mass of earth, a sandheap, or a house so that it falls; to demolish or break a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence covers both causing a mass or structure to fall and demolition by undermining it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring down or ruin a person's dominion, power, or means of support; for such standing to collapse or depart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression ثَلَّ عَرْشُهُ, the result may be loss of power, ruin, or abasement; one interpretation describes a portion or company falling away from him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill or destroy a man or people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive use concerns the destruction of persons; related usage can describe causing someone to die.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die or perish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the intransitive or resultative use of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or cast earth or mud out of a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use includes removing earth from a well and mud from its bottom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast or solid-hoofed animal, to dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is predicated of the animal or its hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rich or financially competent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate intransitive classical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abound in ثَلَّة, whether wool or a flock of sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived verb is Form IV and is predicated of a person possessing much of what is called ثَلَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To order or command the repair of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be something thrown down or demolished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thrown down or demolished; to fall gradually, part after part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence applies this especially to a house and to a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour forth or become poured forth; of people, to stream upon or against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural construction اِنْثَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ describes people pouring themselves forth upon or against another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth or mud taken from a well, including the ground around its mouth; also, a grave filled with earth after digging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These related senses concern earth associated with excavating and refilling a well or grave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clay or mud structure made in the desert for shade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The structure is compared with a small shelter or beacon-like construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wool, especially a gathered quantity of wool; by extension, animal fiber described as wool, goats' hair, or camel hair in various specifications.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical authorities differ over which combinations of wool and other animal hair are included.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A flock of sheep or goats, whether few or many, and in some specifications especially a numerous flock of sheep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records differing specifications concerning sheep, goats, and the size of the flock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Many pieces of money or a large amount of money.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal use distinct from the verb meaning ‘to pour forth money.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: An interval of two days, or abstention from water for two days, between two drinkings by camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This technical use belongs to the terminology of camels coming to water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who remains or stays settled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a rare classical designation associated with the idea of remaining together or settled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death, perdition, or destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can also function as an infinitive associated with killing or destroying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The perishing or passing away of might, power, or elevated condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal expression for the decline of an elevated or powerful state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man abounding in ثَلَّة, such as wool or a flock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is defined through the classical noun ثَلَّة rather than through the Quranic noun ثُلَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A colt that dungs much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This occurs in the phrase مُهْرٌ مِثَلٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Collecting wealth and managing or arranging it well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning includes putting wealth into a good state or condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shortening of the teeth caused by the loss of part of them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an anatomical use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the mouth, to lose its teeth or have its teeth fall out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object of the derived verb is the mouth in this anatomical construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house that has been thrown down or demolished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive participial description of a demolished house.

cautions: The Quranic form ثُلَّة denotes a company or group of people; the wool, flock, money, well-earth, and demolition branches belong to other classical uses and should not be imported into the Quranic sense.

Classical authorities give competing specifications for the composition or scope of ثَلَّة in its wool and flock meanings; these variations are retained without making them restrictions on the Quranic noun.
